positive_text:
Suppose $n \geq 4$ people were seated in a circle yesterday. Each person recalls the identities of the two adjacent people, but not the direction (left or right). Today, you need to reseat the same people around the same circular table so that each person is adjacent to the same two individuals as yesterday (though the direction may be reversed). You can ask any subset of people to identify their two adjacent individuals from yesterday.

a. What is the minimum number $f(n)$ of people you must ask in advance (i.e., without knowing the answers to earlier questions) to ensure you can reconstruct the seating?

b. What is the minimum number $g(n)$ of people you must ask, if you can adaptively choose whom to ask based on previous responses, to guarantee a correct reconstruction?
